page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Head: running title and page number at the top. Below the first line, a division heading "EXERCIT. III." with a subtitle, then the body text. Six printed quotation marks stand in the left margin beside the paragraph, with no text.

main_text.l: humano corpore, nihil esse aliud quàm e[?]-
ius interitum. At hominis formam, quæ di-
uina essentia est, interire, nemo, nisi impius
proferet. Verùm materiales formas, cuius-
modi sunt illæ brutorum, plantarum, & o-
mnium imperfectorum corporum, euane-
scere, ac in nihilum redigi, dum hæc corrum-
puntur, ire inficias minimè uolumus.
EXERCIT. III.
CUR NON CORRUMPI POS-
RErum generabilium & corruptibili-
um materiam non interire, Fernelius
ibidem ingenuè fatetur, sed causas
non appositè uidetur reddere. Si enim (inq-
uit) quando res oblitescit, illius materia
simul interiret & disiparetur, communis
rerum omnium moles iamdudum, uel fæ-
pius esset absorpta, nec hominum uniuer-
sum genus, nec rerum natura omnis, nec i-
pse mundus stare posset. Hæc Fernelij ratio
adeò est infirma, ut nec uerisimilis, nec ap-
parens uideatur. Nam si res, quæ intereunt
in nihilum redigi contingeret, ealdem quo-
que ex nihilo fieri necessariò consequere-
tur.

page.notes: The first word of the body paragraph is a large initial "R" joined to "Rerum". The first line "quàm e-ius" has an unclear letter after "quàm" (read as e, marked [?]). The word "ealdem" and "(inquit)" are as printed. Six small quotation marks stand in the left margin beside the body paragraph; they are printed marks, not text, and are not transcribed. No catchword, signature or footnote is printed. Long s is normalised to s throughout, for example "fcere" to "scere".
